requirement:
Build a URL shortener service as a JSON HTTP API using FastAPI and SQLite.

Endpoints: POST /api/links creates a short link from a long URL and returns the short code. GET /{code} redirects a visitor to the original URL. GET /api/links/{code}/stats returns click analytics for that link. GET /health returns service health.

Access: link creation is unauthenticated for this release. There is no user or API-key subsystem and analytics are public. Abuse is handled by per-IP rate limiting on creation, not by authentication.

Open redirect protection is a denylist, not an allowlist. Any public http or https destination is permitted. Reject any other scheme, and reject any destination resolving to a loopback, private or link-local address, including the cloud metadata address. The service must never fetch the destination itself.

Expiry: a caller may pass an expiry; when omitted the link expires 30 days after creation. Requests for an expired link return 410 Gone.

Analytics: total click count plus timestamp, referrer and user agent per click. Do not store visitor IP addresses.

Short codes are randomly generated, not sequential, so that links cannot be enumerated.
demonstrates: decomposition of a clear requirement into a dependency graph
parallel execution of implementation, test authoring and documentation
a real pytest run as the verification gate, not a claimed one

ambiguities.question: When the service runs behind a reverse proxy or CDN, should the rate limiter derive the client IP from X-Forwarded-For, or only from the direct socket peer address?
ambiguities.why: Trusting X-Forwarded-For unconditionally lets any caller bypass the rate limit with a spoofed header; using only the socket address collapses every proxied request onto one bucket and rate-limits the whole internet as a single client.

ambiguities.question: What are the exact rate limit numbers (requests per window per IP)?
ambiguities.why: Determines the threshold constant and the values used in the 429 acceptance test, but not the design of the limiter.

ambiguities.question: Should submitting the same long URL twice return the existing code or mint a new one?
ambiguities.why: Deduplication changes the create path (lookup-before-insert) and the uniqueness guarantees callers can rely on.

ambiguities.question: Is 307 the required redirect status, or should 301/302 be used?
ambiguities.why: 301 is cached by browsers and would silently stop click analytics and expiry enforcement; 302 vs 307 differs only in method-preservation semantics.

ambiguities.question: Should DNS-based destination validation be repeated at redirect time, or performed only at creation time?
ambiguities.why: Creation-time-only validation leaves a DNS rebinding window where a host that resolved publicly later points at an internal address; re-validating on every redirect adds a resolver call to the hot path.

ambiguities.question: Is there a maximum allowed caller-supplied expiry (e.g. one year), or may a caller request an arbitrarily distant expiry?
ambiguities.why: A cap adds a validation branch and a 400 case; without one, links are effectively permanent and storage grows unbounded.

ambiguities.question: Should expired links and their click rows be purged, or retained indefinitely for analytics?
ambiguities.why: Purging requires a background job and makes stats for expired links eventually 404 instead of 200.
